instructions: Put the 8 eggs in a saucepan and cover them with cold water by an inch. Bring it to a boil over high heat.
As soon as it boils, turn the heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes.
While the eggs cook, finely chop the 2 onions and the 4 tomatoes. Grate 1 tsp of the ginger and mince the 2 garlic cloves. Slice the green chili thinly and put it in a small bowl for the table.
Drain the eggs and cover them with cold water. Leave them for 5 minutes, then peel them and pat them dry. Prick each egg 2 or 3 times with a fork.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the eggs and turn them every minute or so for 3 to 4 minutes, until they're golden with a few blistered spots. Stand back a little. They can spatter.
Move the eggs to a plate and sprinkle them with 1/4 tsp of the salt.
Add the remaining 2 tbsp oil to the same pan with the bay leaf, the cinnamon and the 2 cardamom pods. After about 20 seconds they'll sizzle and smell warm.
Add the onions and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until they're golden. Don't rush the onions. They give the gravy its body.
Stir in the ginger and garlic and cook for about a minute, until they stop smelling raw.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, mashing them with the spoon, until they turn mushy.

Turn the heat to medium low. Add the 1 tsp chili powder, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp ground coriander, 1/4 tsp turmeric and the remaining 3/4 tsp salt. Stir for 2 to 3 minutes, until it smells toasty and the masala pulls away from the sides of the pan. If it starts to stick, add a splash of water.
Pour in 1 1/2 cups water and scrape up anything stuck to the bottom. Cover and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, until the gravy has thickened and you can see little spots of oil on top.
Add the eggs and crush the 1/2 tsp kasuri methi between your palms over the pan. Simmer for 3 minutes, spooning the gravy over the eggs.
Chop 2 tbsp of the cilantro and scatter it over the top. Taste the gravy. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with roti, naan or rice, with the sliced green chili on the side.
method_notes: All three simmer hard boiled eggs in an onion, ginger garlic and tomato gravy built on whole spices in oil or ghee, with chili, coriander, turmeric and garam masala. Swasthi's (the dhaba style version) pricks the boiled eggs and fries them golden before they go in, then finishes with kasuri methi and an optional splash of cream or cashew milk. Cook with Manali tempers cumin, mustard seeds, cloves and peppercorns and adds green peas; My Food Story grinds the onion, ginger, garlic, chili and cilantro to a paste first and fries the slit eggs in turmeric and salt. This one follows Swasthi's, doubled to 8 eggs for four, without the cream, and with the chili on the side.
